events.title: Civil War History in Oakton and Vienna
events.description: Greater Oakton Community Association invites history enthusiasts to join a narrated historic bus tour led by acclaimed local historian Jim Lewis on from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Please arrive at 9:00 a.m. at Oakton Community Park at 2841 Hunter Mill Road (next to the old schoolhouse and roundabout) for Jim Lewis's opening comments, then board the bus for departure by 9:30 a.m. The tour will end at 1:00 p.m. This 3.5-hour journey spans Fairfax County's history from its formation in 1742 through the early 1900s, focusing on sites primarily on or just off Hunter Mill Road. Participants hear stories of where the old mills and roads were located and learn about famed military figures (particularly from the Civil War era) and colorful residents who graced the area. Numerous period photographs support the narrative, bringing history to life. Walking requirements are minimal, although one segment involves going down a slight grassy decline. The tour runs rain or shine. Snacks and water are included. Cost is $45 per seat. In the event of cancellation, refunds are provided if a replacement is found for the seat; a wait list is maintained for this purpose. There are 23 seats on the bus. Special "Event Pricing" is offered for the award-winning "Danger Between the Lines" DVD and tour-related illustrated books, available for purchase with cash only. Narrated Historic Bus Tour with Jim Lewis combines local history education, community connection, and immersive storytelling in Fairfax County, Virginia. Questions? Email contact@greateroakton.com . events.description: History, Heroics, and the Occasional Amputation (Strictly Metaphorical) Right, gather round, you historically curious lot! Step smartly aboard as we begin our highly educational meander from the National Museum of Civil War Medicine in Downtown Frederick, Maryland, where you’ll learn how doctors once treated nearly everything with brandy, saws, and an unwavering sense of optimism. Your guide, a certified docent and part-time time traveler, will regale you with tales of battlefield brilliance, questionable hygiene, and the astonishing resilience of people who really ought to have taken the day off. So join us for a Frederick Civil War history tour because this isn’t just history… it’s history on the double, with a head wound and a bandage made from curtains. Perfect for history buffs, museum lovers, and anyone searching for unique things to do in Frederick, Maryland, this unforgettable Civil War bus tour offers a delightfully British take on America’s most dramatic century.

events.title: Haunted History at The National Museum of Civil War Medicine
events.venue: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
events.description: Starting on October 10th, tour the most haunted building in Frederick – the National Museum of Civil War Medicine. Explore the building’s history amidst the darkened galleries and offices. On the tour, staff and volunteers will share stories of Civil War embalmers, the building’s most infamous tenants, and their first-hand accounts of paranormal activity that have given the building its spooky reputation. In addition to a trip through the museum galleries, the tour provides exclusive access to the third floor where numerous sightings have occurred. 48 East Patrick Street was built in the 1830s. Before it became the National Museum of Civil War Medicine, the building was a furniture shop and a site of Civil War embalming, as well as home to many Frederick residents and their businesses. The past still echoes through the halls of the building. The haunting sights, sounds, and sensations from the building have been reported for decades by the people who lived and worked in the building over many years. Join us to hear our staff and volunteers’ stories first-hand. You are invited to bring your own cameras and ghost-finding apps – who knows what you’ll capture! Flash photography and LIVE streaming are prohibited. Tours will be given on October 10, 17, 24, and 25, from 5:30 p.m.-6:30 p.m. This year we are offering two special Halloween tours on Saturday, October 31, from 5:30 p.m.-8:00 p.m. and 8:00 p.m.-10:30 p.m. During these special Halloween night tours, you’ll have additional time to tour the galleries without a guide.

events.description: Two decks, one timeline, and absolutely no sense of direction. Good morning, historians, adventurers, and anyone who got on the wrong bus but is too polite to admit it! Prepare yourself for an extraordinary expedition aboard our towering yellow vintage London double-decker bus, now thundering proudly through the streets of Downtown Frederick, Maryland. You’ll start your day along the scenic Carroll Creek Park, where our gleaming double-decker waits like a massive custard-colored teapot on wheels. Once aboard, take your seat, clutch your belongings, and abandon all responsibility, our Clippies will handle the chaos from here. As we trundle through historic Downtown Frederick, you’ll be treated to a fully guided Frederick history tour through centuries of local stories, from colonial shenanigans to architectural brilliance, from Civil War-era landmarks to the occasional ghost who refuses to pay rent. Perfect for families, visitors, history lovers, and anyone looking for fun things to do in Frederick Maryland, this unforgettable historical sightseeing tour is your front-row seat to the city’s remarkable past, served with a generous helping of British wit.

This stop is a highlight among Frederick’s bakery tours, and you’ll quickly understand why it’s a local favourite. Whether you’re a bibliophile, a foodie, or simply looking for unique things to do in Frederick, Maryland, Pages & Pastries is the perfect combination of books, bakeries, and double-decker bus charm. It’s a Frederick city tour for the curious, the hungry, and the happily confused, mixing stories, sweets, and scenic streets into one gloriously crumb-covered adventure. Come hungry. events.description: "Remember the Ladies: An America 250 Concert" 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence during a critical year in the American Revolution—1776. Join the City of Fairfax Theatre Company for a unique musical reflection on America 250 through the lens of women’s history: “Remember the Ladies: An America 250 Concert.” Through story and song, an all-female cast will present a selection of pieces that consider the many aspects of what it means to be an American. events.title: Hermit Day
events.description: Hermit Day October 29 @ 9:30 am - 4:00 pm Day of Quiet at Bon Secours Do you… need a day of quiet and solitude to rest, reflect, be? need at least one of these each year? sense that God may be inviting you to enter silence and reorient? October 29 th might be just for you, as it is the annual celebration of National Hermit Day. Although its origins are not firmly known, many attribute Hermit Day’s origin to the 18th century and suggest a connection to the Irish Hermit Saint Colman. It gives us an opportunity to join the many others who — throughout Christian history — have entered silence and solitude to remember what is most important: to listen, to pray. A day like this has the potential to initiate or strengthen a regular practice. On this guided tour of the William Paca House and Garden, explore the origins of customs and practices once accepted as fact and, in some cases, still observed today. From household rituals to good-luck charms and protective practices, uncover the meanings behind these enduring traditions and learn how they influenced daily life. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. events.title: Legends & Lore
events.description: Come see the darker side of Frederick. When night falls, Frederick’s familiar streets have rather different stories to tell. Climb aboard our vintage double-decker for an hour of dark tales from Frederick’s past , researched from local histories, old accounts and the legends that have lingered long after the people involved have gone. As we make our way through the city, we’ll slow down at the very places connected to these stories, from historic streets and old buildings to some of Frederick’s more famously haunted places . Along the way, you’ll hear tales of strange happenings, restless spirits and the darker chapters of local history, all told against the backdrop of Frederick after dark. And because it’s October, you’ll also get a rather good view from the top deck as the city’s historic homes and neighborhoods put on their best autumn and Halloween displays. Whether you’re a believer, a skeptic, or simply enjoy a good story with a slightly unsettling ending, Legends and Lore offers a different way to discover Frederick’s history. Just remember, it’s much easier to laugh at a ghost story when you’re not sitting on the top deck in the dark. TOUR HIGHLIGHTS Hear researched tales of Frederick’s haunted places, local legends and darker history, told where the stories happened. Experience Frederick after dark from the top deck, with historic streets, autumn displays and a few places you’ll look at rather differently afterwards. TOUR DETAILS Price: $35 per person Duration: 1 hour Recommended Age: 14+ Departure: RAK Brewing Co, 400 Sagner Ave, Frederick, MD, 21701

events.title: African American Quilt Documentation Day in DC
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts - Great Hall
events.address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005-3970
events.description: WASHINGTON, DC — The African American Quilt Documentation Study Group (AAQDSG) will host a FREE quilt documentation event in Washington, DC on Sunday, November 1, 2026, inviting the African American community to bring family quilts in to be documented, preserved, and honored as part of our shared history. Date: Sunday, November 1, 2026 Time: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Location: National Museum of Women in the Arts, 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005 Cost: Free — pre-registration required (time slots are limited) Since the 1980s, quilt documentation has been used to preserve family legacies and record the social, cultural, and artistic significance of quilts. African American family quilts have historically been excluded from this process. Most exist today with no documented history of the quilt or its maker — what's known has been passed down orally and never recorded. "Documentation is how we hold onto that," said A'donna Richardson, Director of AAQDSG. "It's an act of honoring our ancestors, of making sure the work of the quilt maker's hands is remembered. It's a way of saying: our ancestors mattered, what they made matters, and the stories tied to their quilts matter." The process reaches beyond individual families. Documented quilts become part of the historical record that scholars, museums, and researchers rely on to understand African American creativity, survival, faith, and community. Without this work, those stories remain untold and the historical record remains misrepresented and incomplete. We are encouraging the African American community to bring their family quilts, in whatever condition (the older, the better), to the November 1 event to have them photographed and documented, and to share the stories behind them. YOU MUST REGISTER to attend: https://aaqdsg.org/events If all appointment slots are filled, send your name and contact information to afamquilydoc@aadqsg.org. events.description: Welcome to L eech Woods According to Montgomery County historical land records, the present site of Leech Woods was originally settled by Warwick and Jeanne Leech and their six children sometime in early 1790. Having immigrated from Hungary, the family chose Damascus, Maryland, based on its temperate climate and heavily wooded region, which reminded them of their homeland. The Leech family store thrived as the leading local merchant of hides, furs, and hunting supplies. During the disastrous Winter of 1804, the Leech family store was robbed and vandalized by unknown attackers and the body of John Leech, the youngest son, was found nailed to the back wall of the store. The remaining bodies of the family members were later found bludgeoned and bound inside of the root cellar of their homestead. No further information about the attackers or motives for the killings is known. ​ Remnants of the Leech family homestead still stand deep in the woods where the present Leech Woods experience is built. The Leech Woods immersive experience follows the original walking path from the site of the Leech family hunting supply store to the remnants of the original family homestead. As the property was classified as a historical site in 1972, no artifacts may be removed, and we ask that you respect the privacy of the grave sites. What’s new? More Scares. More scenes. More Screams. We added 6 new scenes to the original trail to bring you even more terror. The Horror Hayride also has new scenes added to the 20-minute ride/walk-through. What to expect Leech Woods is a thirty-minute immersive haunted trail experience of dark terror. We promise a night of chainsaws, clowns, and dark corners. When you are done screaming, we offer amazing food and drinks, alcoholic beverages, bonfires, glow-in-the-dark axe-throwing, fire dancers, a DJ booth, fortune telling, and other forms of entertainment every night in the Leech Woods Midway, where Admission Is Free. Trail What is our Trail? Leech Woods is one of the scariest haunted trails in all of Maryland. It’s about a 30-minute walk with now over 15 highly detailed immersive walkthrough scenes, all enhanced this year with even more scares. Plus, our trail has over 50 professionally trained scarers. You can check out our gallery to see photos of our trail and actors. Recommend age: 12+ HORROR HAYRIDE What is the Horror Hayride? The Horror Hayride is a 20-minute ride and walk-through full of brand new, highly detailed, immersive scenes. On this trail, you discover what is believed to be the Leech Woods family cemetery. Limited to 25 victims per trip. Please respect the graves and reserve your seats now. ​ Recommended Age: 12+ Tickets 15% OFF Groups of 5 Or More Use Code “GROUP”

Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Immerse yourself in the daily life of soldiers, military officers, and the camp followers who traveled with the army as you explore a Revolutionary War encampment. At this hands-on attraction, you can touch the items inside the soldiers' tents and officer's tent, wash clothes in the laundry yard, and examine cooking utensils used by camp followers. See two daily programs about enlisting in General Washington's army and how soldiers prepared their meals while traveling. This attraction is made possible thanks to Americana Corner.

These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings.
